question.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{6}),$ calculate $P(X>3).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{6}).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}{e}^{-x/6}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(X>3)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>3) & ={\int }_{3}^{\infty }f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{\infty }\frac{1}{6}{e}^{-x/6}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-{e}^{-x/6}|}_{3}^{\infty } \\  & ={e}^{-1/2} \\  & ≈0.6065\end{aligned}
$$
